title: One body, many parts (1 Corinthians 12:12–27)
hookLine: the eye can't say to the hand, I don't need you
tomorrow: what would Paul tell a room where everyone talks at once?

lines: IS IT THEREFORE NOT OF THE BODY?
cards: Stub a toe on the bed frame in the dark and the whole body stops. Eyes water, hands grab, a word comes out you didn't plan. One small part, and everything answers.

Paul writes a scene where a foot tries to quit: "Because I am not the hand, I am not of the body." An ear joins in: I'm not the eye, so I don't belong. Paul's reply is one question: "is it therefore not of the body?"

teach.b: He sets it up: "For as the body is one, and hath many members," then the twist: "so also is Christ." Who's in it?

"For by one Spirit are we all baptized into one body, whether we be Jews or Gentiles, whether we be bond or free." A church split over leaders and dinner is told it is one body. Then Paul lets the senses argue.
"If the whole body were an eye, where were the hearing? If the whole were hearing, where were the smelling?" A giant eyeball can't hear a thing.

Then the proud parts: "And the eye cannot say unto the hand, I have no need of thee: nor again the head to the feet, I have no need of you." No part gets to opt out, and no part gets to push another out.
Then he turns the ranking over: "those members of the body, which seem to be more feeble, are necessary." One to tell a friend tonight: in Paul's picture, the stubbed toe is the point.
"Whether one member suffer, all the members suffer with it; or one member be honoured, all the members rejoice with it." Pain travels. So does joy.
"Now ye are the body of Christ, and members in particular." Not a club with members. A body with limbs.

how: Christians call the church the body of Christ, from this chapter; some churches read it when they ordain, baptize or welcome new members.

o: a group where everyone is exactly alike
a single leader who speaks for everyone
many different people joined into one

p: because I am not the hand
all the members suffer with it

s: Paul says the strongest-looking parts of the body matter most
he turns that over: those members which seem to be more feeble, are necessary.
in Paul's picture, when one part suffers, all suffer with it
and when one is honored, all rejoice with it.
Paul says a part that feels left out isn't really part of the body
the foot says it, and Paul answers: is it therefore not of the body?

games.q: the youth band's drummer says she's 'just the drummer' and skips planning meetings, since the singers decide everything. what fits Paul's picture?
o: she's needed at the table: no part can say, I have no need of you.
she's right: some parts are only there to follow the head.
she should learn to sing first, so that she counts as much.
games.why: Paul's foot says because I am not the hand, I am not of the body. his answer: is it therefore not of the body? feeling minor doesn't make you spare.

practice: Press your palms together, then let them rest. Wiggle your toes, and feel your feet on the floor, your back against the chair, the breath moving all of it at once.
Then bring to mind one person very unlike you, and name one thing they bring that you never could. If you pray, you can thank God for them by name.

wordCard.voice: One body. Paul's picture of a church: many members, very different, one Spirit, and none of them spare.

orig.note: Greek: members, the limbs and parts of a body. Paul's word in members in particular.

carryVoice: Hold onto this: every part needed, even the ones that seem feeble or sit far from the front. Go well.
